The 10,222nd meeting of the Security Council is called to order. The provisional agenda for this meeting is the situation in the Middle East. The agenda is adopted. The representative of Russia has asked for the floor. I give him the floor.

Mr. President, We are again compelled to take the floor on a point of order in order to object to yet another unilateral decision by the French Presidency to change the established principle governing the order of speakers at a meeting of the Security Council. This decision was again taken unilaterally, in spite of protests and without any consultation with Council members. We would like to emphasize that the issue is not the particular delegation that the presidency has placed at the top of the list ahead of council members, but rather the selective approach of the Security Council presidency, which has decided that it has some kind of special right to break with long-established practice. We recall that a similar situation arose at the very beginning of September during the council's discussion of the Syrian chemical file, by the way. We did not hear any kind of clear or convincing arguments from our French colleagues then or now. Instead, we were simply told of a certain interpretation of presidential note 507. However, that note in fact states that, quote, "Those who have a direct interest in the outcome of the matter under discussion may speak prior to Council members if this is considered to be appropriate." However, nowhere does it indicate that this kind of decision can be made by the Presidency unilaterally. Our French colleagues pay such close attention to the issue of the Council's working methods, and thus they are keenly aware that the President of the Council does not have special rights, only duties. presidency is required to strictly discharge his or her duties in accordance with the provisional rules of procedure and established practice of this body. In addition, France, as one of the permanent members of the Security Council, bears additional responsibility to safeguard the Council's traditions and to contribute to its smooth functioning. It's strange that France, after its 69th presidency of the Security Council, on the 70th time suddenly forgot about this. In case the French team does not know about this, or I hope not that the Presidency is not aware of this, we are prepared to hold a seminar for our French colleagues on this topic. And we can do it for free as well. We'd like to note that we fully welcome the presence of our Yemeni colleagues at this meeting and are willing to listen to their comments. In keeping with established practice, they will be given the floor under Rule 37 of the Provisional Rules of Procedure of the Security Council. We do not see how changing the speaking order would make their voice carry more weight. In addition, as shown by the discussion on the situation in Yemen last week, the position of the Yemeni colleagues who spoke after Council members was very clearly conveyed. Equally unconvincing are our French colleagues' arguments that such a selective approach would help to optimize the Council's discussions. Colleagues, the speaking order has long been established for specific agenda items and agreed upon by all members of the Council. Any changes to it are not a decision that should be made by the President of the Council automatically, but ought to be the outcome of discussion with all Council members. These kinds of actions simply set a dangerous precedent under which certain delegations are granted the right to speak preferentially at the top of the list of speakers, while others are denied that same right. So we call on the French presidency to think about what they're doing and not to test our patience and that of other delegations with this unilateral and disrespectful attitude toward other Council members. Thank you.
I thank the representative of Russia for that statement and now give the floor to China.

President, inviting the countries concerned to participate in Security Council meetings is an important working method of the Council. China has consistently maintained that when discussing relevant issues, the Council should give due attention to the views of the countries concerned. China also respects the discretion of the President of the Security Council in conducting meetings. At the same time, we believe that making an exception is one thing, and forming an established practice is another. With regard to procedural arrangements such as the order of speakers, the President should respect long-established practice and make decisions by consensus after full consultation with Council members, based on the Rules of Procedure. The fact that a permanent member of the Security Council has repeatedly expressed concerns on this matter warrants serious consideration in order to better preserve the Council's unity and cooperation. I would also like to emphasize that China's remarks above are not directed at the country concerned or at the subject of today's meeting. China welcomes the representative of Yemen to today's meeting and to make remarks. Thank you, President.

I thank China for those remarks, and I thank the two representatives for their explanations. As indicated, after lengthy discussions with Council members, It was important for the Presidency that the representative of Yemen be able to take the floor immediately after the briefing of the ASG Khairi, in accordance with the spirit and letter of paragraph 36 of the Presidential Note, that is S/2024/507, so that the Council has before it the remarks of the country primarily concerned by this issue. In accordance with Article, with Rule 37 of the Council's provisional procedure, I invite the representatives of Saudi Arabia and Yemen to participate in this meeting. It is so decided. In accordance with Rule 39 of the Council's Provisional Rules of Procedure, I invite Mr. Khaled Khairi, Assistant Secretary-General, Departments of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs and Peace Operations, to participate in this meeting. It is so decided.
